openEMS GPU engine -- test build
================================

This package carries the GPU engine as two plugins in openEMS\plugins:

  openEMS_gpu_hip_nvidia.dll   NVIDIA GPUs, Maxwell (GTX 900) and newer;
                               needs only the NVIDIA driver (527.41 or newer)
  openEMS_gpu_hip_amd.dll      AMD GPUs: RDNA 1 to 4 (RX 5000 to RX 9000,
                               Radeon 780M/890M/8060S), CDNA (Instinct);
                               the HIP runtime of the build comes along in
                               openEMS\plugins, the AMD driver is needed

openEMS itself does not need either: without a usable GPU only the GPU engine
is unavailable.

Running
-------

  openEMS.exe model.xml --engine=gpu -v

or from Python

  FDTD.Run(sim_path, engine='gpu', verbose=1)

With -v (verbose=1) openEMS lists the GPU devices it found and, for every
plugin that could not be used, the reason. With more than one GPU the
discrete one with the most memory is taken; --engine=gpu --gpu-device=N
(Python: gpu_device=N) picks another one from the list.

What to report
--------------

Please report at https://github.com/thliebig/openEMS/issues or the forum:

  - GPU, driver version, Windows version
  - the output of a run with -v, especially the "GPU devices:" list and any
    "GPU_Backend::New" lines
  - for a simulation that runs: the speed (MCells/s) of the GPU engine and of
    the default engine, and whether the results agree
